label: Timelines Side by Side
title: Four views of the end times on one line
intro: Each lane follows one view of the millennium through the same events. Shaded bands mark what all four affirm; the gaps and spans show where they part ways.
image_title: Four evangelical views of the end times, side by side
image_subtitle: Shaded columns: what all four views affirm.
image_subtitle_narrow: Shaded rows: what all four views affirm. Dispensational and historic are both premillennial views.
caption: All four lanes begin at the cross and end in the new creation, with Christ's return and a final judgment in between. They differ on what the thousand years of Revelation 20 are, and so on how far apart the return and the final judgment sit.
common_text: All four affirm Christ's death, resurrection and ascension, his personal return, a final judgment, and the new heavens and new earth. Sam Storms, an amillennialist, calls the millennium a secondary issue: "What unites us is our common confession that Jesus is coming back!"

Seven years; the church in heaven

proponent.name: Dallas Theological Seminary
proponent.work: Doctrinal Statement, Articles XVIII to XXI

segments.text: The millennium is now: Christ reigns with his saints while the church suffers
segments.short: Millennium now: Christ reigns with his saints

segments.text: The millennium comes first: the gospel wins multitudes, Israel included

differ: When Christ returns: before the thousand years (both premillennial views) or after them (amillennial and postmillennial).
What the thousand years are: a future reign on earth, Christ's present reign with his saints, or an age of gospel advance before the return.
The rapture: only dispensationalism places a coming for the church before the tribulation, separate from the return to earth.
Israel: dispensationalism expects national Israel restored in the millennium; postmillennialists expect many ethnic Israelites to come to Christ.
Return and judgment: one event for amillennialists and postmillennialists, a thousand years apart for premillennialists.
method: Lane sequences follow Keith Mathison's survey of the four views and each view's own statement listed here.

sources.title: Doctrinal Statement
sources.quote: the next great event in the fulfillment of prophecy will be the coming of the Lord in the air
sources.notes: Article XVIII (coming in the air before the tribulation), XIX (the church in heaven during Israel's seventieth week), XX (return to earth introduces the millennial age, Israel restored to her land), XXI (great white throne at the close of the millennium). sources.title: The Millennial Maze
sources.quote: Books supporting this view have been published by men such as Loraine Boettner, J. Marcellus Kik, Kenneth Gentry, John Jefferson Davis, and myself.
sources.notes: November 25, 2013, first published in Tabletalk. Summarizes all four views; the lane sequences follow it (historic: tribulation, return, righteous raised, reign on earth, the unrighteous raised for judgment; dispensational: rapture, seven-year tribulation, return, rule from Jerusalem, great white throne; postmillennial: the Spirit draws unprecedented multitudes, ethnic Israelites included, then return, general resurrection, final judgment; amillennial: Christ reigns with the saints through the present age, marked by suffering, then return, general resurrection, last judgment, new heavens and new earth).
